transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, it’s probably nothing too dramatic, but… I’ve been feeling very tense in my body lately. My neck and shoulders, and even my jaw, are tight almost all the time now. It’s like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to watch TV at night. I thought I should probably get it checked, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things, even when there isn’t a specific reason to be concerned?

Yes… I suppose I do, probably more than I should. It’s not always one big thing, more like my mind keeps hopping around. I’ll start wondering if the contractors missed something in the house, then whether my lesson plans are slipping, or if the robotics kids are falling behind. And then I start thinking maybe I’m letting my wife or my family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.

I know that may sound a bit much… I’m not trying to make a drama of it, but yes, it does happen quite a lot.
Would you say that your worrying happens most days, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific stressors?

Yes… I think most days, if I’m being honest. I wouldn’t say it’s constant every minute, but it does seem to keep cropping up. My mind jumps from the house and whether the contractors missed something, to school things like lesson plans or the robotics students falling behind, and then to whether I’m disappointing my wife or my family by not keeping it all together.

I know everyone worries, of course, but… yes, it’s more than just the odd stressful day, I think.

When you feel this tension in your body, especially in your neck, shoulders, and jaw, does it seem to happen in response to stress or worry, or does it sometimes occur even when you're not particularly stressed about anything?

I think it’s both, really. It’s worse when I’m worrying, but what’s been bothering me is that it’s there even when nothing obvious is happening. My neck and shoulders, and my jaw especially, just feel tight almost all the time now.

I’ll be sitting at my desk or watching TV in the evening, and it’s like my body is still bracing for something bad. I don’t mean to overstate it, but that’s probably what finally made me come in.
Do you feel like you have a hard time controlling or stopping your worrying, even when you try to?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I do try to stop it. I’ll tell myself, “Right, focus on the class in front of you,” and sometimes that helps for a bit.

But then one small thing gets in, like remembering a late invoice or thinking a student might be falling behind, and it sort of sets off a whole chain of what-ifs. Before I know it, I’m going over things I can’t really fix in that moment, and I can’t seem to shut it down properly.

I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you mean, but… yes, it does feel hard to control.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, anyway. I mean, I can get worked up and tense, but I wouldn’t say it suddenly hits me out of nowhere like an attack or anything.

Maybe I’m not explaining that properly, but it’s more of a build-up of worry than a sudden burst of fear, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms, like stomach issues, headaches, or trouble sleeping, that seem to be related to this tension or worry?

I’m not completely sure, to be honest. I haven’t really kept track in that way.

I mean, I do have days where I feel a bit run down, but I wouldn’t want to say it’s definitely connected if I don’t know. With sleep… I suppose I’m not always as rested as I’d like, but again, I don’t know if that’s just normal at my age or from work.

Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you seen a doctor or had any tests done to check if there’s a medical reason for the tension and tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?

Not really, no… I mean, I probably should have mentioned it sooner. The neck and shoulder tightness — and my jaw, actually — that’s sort of what finally made me come in.

It’s there most of the time now, like I’m bracing myself for something, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV in the evening. I haven’t had tests for it or anything, though. I wasn’t sure if it was worth bothering anyone about, if that makes sense.
Do you find it hard to relax, even when you know there’s nothing pressing going on?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

Even when there isn’t anything urgent, I feel sort of wound up most of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. At school I’ll catch myself pacing around the classroom between lessons, or checking my phone for messages from the contractor when I probably don’t need to.

It’s not that I’m panicking exactly… I just don’t seem to properly switch off. Does that make sense?
Has this tension or worrying made it harder for you to do things you need to do, like your work, spending time with family, or relaxing when you want to?

A bit, yes… though I’ve been trying not to let it show too much.

At work, I’ve started falling behind on lesson prep and marking, which isn’t really like me. I’m still getting the important things done, mostly, but it takes me longer, and I find myself putting things off because I feel so wound up.

And outside of work… I usually help manage parts of a community theatre group, and I’ve had to step back from some of that. I just couldn’t keep up with everything anymore. I feel a bit embarrassed saying that, because it sounds like I’m not coping, but… yes, it has started to get in the way.
Do you feel anxious or worried about a number of different things, even when you try not to let it bother you?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just normal life stuff, nothing unusual, but my mind does seem to bounce from one thing to the next.

It’ll be the house, like whether the contractors have missed something, then it’s whether my lesson plans are slipping, or whether the robotics students are falling behind because I’m not on top of it enough. And then I start thinking I’m letting my wife down, or the family generally, by not keeping everything under control.

I know some of that probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, but it does keep going round in my head even when I’m trying not to let it.

Do you find yourself frequently worried or preoccupied with the idea that these physical sensations in your neck, shoulders, or jaw might be signs of a serious illness, even though doctors haven’t found anything wrong?

Not really, no… I mean, I notice the tightness, and it’s unpleasant, but I don’t usually jump to thinking it’s something seriously wrong with me.

I suppose I might wonder if I’m overdoing it or sitting awkwardly, that sort of thing, but I’m not preoccupied with it being an illness. At least, I don’t think so. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you often feel anxious or distressed specifically about these physical sensations in your body, like the tightness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw, even though no medical cause has been found?

I don’t think so, not specifically about the sensations themselves. I mean, they’re annoying, and I’d rather they weren’t there, but I don’t usually get distressed thinking, “What is this?” or anything like that.

It’s more that I notice them and think I’m probably tense or carrying myself badly. But I wouldn’t say I’m anxious about the tightness itself, if that makes sense.
Do you often feel anxious or overwhelmed about many different parts of your life, even when you know logically that everything is okay?

Yes… I suppose I do, more than I’d like to admit. I mean, I know on paper things are mostly okay, and I try to tell myself that, but my head doesn’t really stay with one thing.

It’ll go from worrying whether the contractors have missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are getting away from me, to whether the robotics kids are falling behind because I’m not doing enough. Then I start thinking I’m letting my wife down, or the family down, because I’m not keeping everything properly under control.

I know that probably sounds a bit over the top, but it does feel overwhelming sometimes.
Do you often experience a general sense of anxiety or dread about many areas of your life, even when there isn't a clear reason for concern?

Yes… I think that’s probably fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I do manage, but there’s often this sort of low-level dread that moves around.

My mind keeps jumping from one thing to another — whether the contractors have missed something in the house, whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are falling behind… and then I start thinking I’m disappointing my wife or my family because I’m not keeping everything under control.

Even when there isn’t one clear disaster happening, it can feel like there’s always something I should be worrying about. Does that make sense?

It’s more that I notice them and think I’m probably tense or carrying myself badly. But I wouldn’t say I’m anxious about the tightness itself, if that makes sense.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences persistent and excessive anxiety about multiple everyday issues beyond the physical symptoms, which would support generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) over somatic symptom disorder (F45.42).
doctor.question: Do you often feel anxious or overwhelmed about many different parts of your life, even when you know logically that everything is okay?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: My mind keeps jumping from whether the contractors missed something in the house to whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are behind, and whether I'm disappointing my wife and family by not keeping everything under control.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about persistent anxiety and worry across many different areas of life, which directly matches excessive anxiety and worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
Yes… I suppose I do, more than I’d like to admit. I mean, I know on paper things are mostly okay, and I try to tell myself that, but my head doesn’t really stay with one thing.

It’ll go from worrying whether the contractors have missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are getting away from me, to whether the robotics kids are falling behind because I’m not doing enough. Then I start thinking I’m letting my wife down, or the family down, because I’m not keeping everything properly under control.

I know that probably sounds a bit over the top, but it does feel overwhelming sometimes.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences persistent and excessive anxiety about multiple events or activities, which is a key feature of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1), as opposed to Persistent Somatoform Pain Disorder (F45.42), which is primarily focused on pain symptoms that cannot be fully explained by a medical condition.
doctor.question: Do you often experience a general sense of anxiety or dread about many areas of your life, even when there isn't a clear reason for concern?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: My mind keeps jumping from whether the contractors missed something in the house to whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are behind, and whether I'm disappointing my wife and family by not keeping everything under control.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about persistent, generalized anxiety or dread across many areas of life, which directly matches excessive anxiety and worry about multiple events or activities.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think that’s probably fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I do manage, but there’s often this sort of low-level dread that moves around.

My mind keeps jumping from one thing to another — whether the contractors have missed something in the house, whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are falling behind… and then I start thinking I’m disappointing my wife or my family because I’m not keeping everything under control.

Even when there isn’t one clear disaster happening, it can feel like there’s always something I should be worrying about. Does that make sense?

inference.note: The patient consistently reports excessive worry across multiple domains, difficulty controlling worry, and associated physical symptoms (muscle tension), without evidence of panic attacks, preoccupation with physical symptoms as signs of illness, or features of other anxiety disorders. This supports Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) as the primary diagnosis.
